title: Finite scalar restriction and pro-etale adjunction units
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a unital homomorphism of finite rings, neither assumed commutative. Use compatible small pro-etale sites, coefficient sheaves $R_T,S_T$ and categories of left module sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The maps $\varphi_T:R_T\to S_T$ are induced by pointwise composition with $\varphi$ on continuous functions and sheafification. Let $P_T:\operatorname{Mod}(S_T)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $C=R,S$, let $f_C^*$ be the inverse image with transported action [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] through the canonical ring isomorphism $c^C_f:f^{-1}C_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}C_X$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and let $f_{C,*}$ be direct image with scalar action through the adjunct $C_Y\to f_*C_X$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the module adjunctions induced by the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction on abelian sheaves, and denote their units by $\eta^C$.

There are natural isomorphisms
$$\alpha_N:P_X(f_S^*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}f_R^*(P_YN),\qquad
\beta_M:P_Y(f_{S,*}M)\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{R,*}(P_XM),$$
for every $S_Y$-module sheaf $N$ and $S_X$-module sheaf $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Their underlying abelian-sheaf maps are the identity under the displayed constructions. They preserve the specified adjunction unit: for every $N$,
$$f_{R,*}(\alpha_N)\circ\beta_{f_S^*N}\circ P_Y(\eta^S_N)=\eta^R_{P_YN}.$$
No flatness, immersion, Noetherian, support or constructibility assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules: lifting the abelian adjunction and its unit; agent coefficient-naturality refinement for the transported-action finite-ring inverse images (noncommutative rings included).

proof.text: For each C=R,S, the coefficient map c^C_f:f^{-1}C_Y -> C_X is the constant-section isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] says that f_C^*N is f^{-1}N with its action transported through this map. The underlying abelian sheaf of P_X(f_S^*N) is therefore the same f^{-1}N as that of f_R^*(P_YN). On a local constant scalar, both transported actions send r in R_X to the action of its image in S_X, because c^S_f composed with f^{-1}(varphi_Y) equals varphi_X composed with c^R_f as ring maps f^{-1}R_Y -> S_X. To see this equality, pass to adjuncts under the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]: by naturality of the adjunction the two adjuncts are rho^S composed with varphi_Y and f_*(varphi_X) composed with rho^R, as maps R_Y -> f_*S_X, where rho^C is the map of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] whose adjoint is c^C_f. On a constant section a over W -> Y both give the constant section varphi(a) of S_X over W x_Y X, because rho sends a to the constant section a and varphi_X is pointwise composition with varphi; an element of the defining presheaf Cont(pi_0(|W|),R) is constant on the members of an open cover of W, so both maps agree on it by gluing, and hence on the sheafification R_Y by its universal property. Also f^{-1}(P_YN) is f^{-1}N with action map f^{-1} of the composite of varphi_Y x id with the S_Y-action, since f^{-1} preserves finite products [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The identity on the underlying abelian sheaf is consequently R_X-linear, giving the natural isomorphism alpha_N; its same identity is the inverse. The restriction action and linearity are exactly [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, together with the coefficient-action definitions in proetale.tex Tag 09A5

proof.text: For an S_X-module sheaf M, the underlying abelian sheaves of P_Y(f_{S,*}M) and f_{R,*}(P_XM) are both the sectionwise direct image V maps to M(u_f(V)) from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. On an object V to Y, the R_Y(V)-action on the first object applies varphi_Y and then the map rho^S_V:S_Y(V) -> S_X(u_f(V)); the action on the second applies rho^R_V:R_Y(V) -> R_X(u_f(V)) and then varphi_X. Here rho^C:C_Y -> f_*C_X is the adjunct of c^C_f defined in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. The equality rho^S varphi_Y = f_*(varphi_X) rho^R was checked in step 1: the two maps agree on constant sections by the pointwise definition of varphi, hence on the defining presheaf by gluing over an open cover and after sheafification. Thus the identity underlying map is R_Y-linear, yielding the natural isomorphism beta_M, again with identity inverse. This uses the restriction-of-scalars construction of [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and the sectionwise module morphisms of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, with proetale.tex Tag 09A5 direct-image action

proof.text: The module adjunctions in the statement are the abelian-sheaf inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions with the transported actions: [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives the same underlying unit eta_f, and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] says that a module morphism is determined by its underlying abelian-sheaf map. By the first two steps, alpha_N and beta_{f_S^*N} have identity underlying maps. Restriction of scalars also leaves underlying sheaves and maps unchanged by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Hence the underlying abelian map of f_{R,*}(alpha_N) composed with beta_{f_S^*N} composed with P_Y(eta^S_N) is exactly the abelian adjunction unit eta_f on P_YN, which is the underlying map of eta^R_{P_YN}. Faithfulness of the forgetful description in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] then gives the displayed equality of R_Y-module morphisms. No flatness or commutativity was used.

No new nodes were needed.

The parent lem-exc-proetale-supported-kernel-complex uses the item for Z/n -> A exactly as stated. The mathematics is correct. Step 1 holds because the identity is R_X-linear exactly when c^S∘f^{-1}φ_Y = φ_X∘c^R. Step 2 needs the equivalent equality ρ^S φ_Y = f_*(φ_X) ρ^R. Step 3's unit equation holds because every underlying map is the identity or η_f and the forgetful functor is faithful. Small cases checked: X empty, R = 0, φ = id, and noncommutative M_2(F_p). Fixes (no new nodes, statement unchanged): (1) Step 1 only gestured at the coefficient-map equality. I wrote out the argument: pass to adjuncts, check on constant sections, glue over an open cover, then use sheafification. I also wrote out that f^{-1}(P_Y N) carries the f^{-1}-transformed restricted action, since f^{-1} preserves finite products. (2) Step 2 cited def-weil-proetale-inverse-image for ρ, but that node defines ρ only for commutative constant A. I added the missing citation of prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, which defines ρ for noncommutative pro-étale coefficients. Tool uses for the maintainer to record: prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map and prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact (unit sk-thm-properbasechange).
